# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — mta-2024-08-15

## Evidence Reviewed
`2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, capture window 2024-08-15 04:09:43–04:42:26 UTC+4, ~33 min). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived entirely from packet-level analysis via tshark.

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 (DHCP-leased from server 10.8.15.4; earlier NAK'd request for 10.8.15.132) |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString and NBNS/Kerberos traffic to DC WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) |

## Infection Chain (chronological)
1. **04:10:58** — Browser (Edge/Chrome 127, victim host) requests `GET /managements?...` from **quote.checkfedexexp.com** (resolving to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare-fronted). Response body is a ZIP archive containing `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`, a ~7 MB JScript file padded almost entirely with junk filler text (book/document excerpts) to inflate its size and evade signature/heuristic detection — a fake-invoice/tracking-page JS downloader.
2. **04:11:59** — Host issues a `Microsoft BITS/7.8` HEAD/GET for `/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` directly against **72.5.43.29** (raw IP, no DNS lookup precedes it — the address is hardcoded). Retrieves a 159,232-byte **PE32+ x86-64 DLL**.
   - SHA256: `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`
3. **04:13:00 onward** — Host begins persistent HTTP beaconing to **72.5.43.29:80**, ~306 requests over the remainder of the capture (roughly every 5–7 seconds). Each request carries a fixed, malformed User-Agent (`Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` — note the space in "Mozilla / 5.0") and a large base64-style blob in the `Cookie` header (bot ID/session token). Responses and POST bodies are opaque encrypted/binary data, not HTML. This is the C2 check-in/task loop.

Note: concurrent BITS transfers to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` (Windows Update CDN) and TeamViewer/Windows Defender update files pulled in the same window are legitimate background OS/AV traffic, unrelated to the compromise — verified by destination and file identity (am_delta_patch, TeamViewer installer components).

## Malware Family
**Behavioral attribution: consistent with Latrodectus (loader)** — not signature-confirmed, since no IDS/AV alert artifacts were included in this evidence set to corroborate via rule/signature hit. The attribution rests on TTP overlap observed directly in traffic:
- Fake shipping/invoice-tracking lure domain serving an oversized, junk-padded `.js` downloader inside a ZIP.
- Abuse of the native Windows BITS service (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` UA) to fetch a second-stage DLL from a hardcoded C2 IP with no DNS resolution.
- Post-infection HTTP beaconing using a fixed, malformed legacy-IE user-agent string with an encrypted `Cookie`-header token and encrypted binary GET/POST bodies to the same C2 IP over plain HTTP.

Treat this as behavioral/TTP-based attribution pending sandbox detonation or AV/YARA confirmation of the extracted DLL.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded C2 IP, no associated DNS record observed; ~306 beacon requests to `GET /` and `POST /`.

**Malicious/lure domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159)

**Malicious URL (initial payload delivery)**
- `hxxp://quote.checkfedexexp[.]com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
- `hxxp://72.5.43[.]29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (second-stage DLL fetch via BITS)

**Transferred files**
| File | Detail |
|---|---|
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | 6,990,020 bytes, inside ZIP from quote.checkfedexexp.com; junk-padded JScript downloader |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | 159,232 bytes, PE32+ DLL, SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`, retrieved via BITS from 72.5.43.29 |

**Distinctive beacon fingerprint**
- User-Agent: `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the space after "Mozilla") — usable as a network detection signature for this host/campaign.
